note: Literature establishes GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 loss-of-function variants as causing neurodevelopmental syndromes presenting with spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability, and epilepsy, differentiating them from pure hereditary spastic paraplegia.

evidence.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in GTPBP1 and GTPBP2 present with a complex neurodevelopmental phenotype featuring developmental delay with or without epilepsy, spastic paraplegia, or motor neuropathy.
